policy_items.question: Based on France’s statement of 9 December 2021, what role should the Security Council play in addressing climate-related insecurity? Explain why a response limited to armed forces and peacekeepers would be insufficient, and identify one complementary measure France supported.

criteria.description: Describe a Council role in anticipating, assessing, preventing or addressing climate-related security risks.
support_quotes: The Security Council must be able to anticipate, prevent and seek solutions to counter the effects of climate change

criteria.description: Explain that armed forces/peacekeepers alone are insufficient; understanding climate–crisis links and building resilience are also needed.
support_quotes: we cannot rely solely on the commitment of the armed forces and peacekeepers
we also need a way to better understand how climate change and crises are linked

criteria.description: Give at least one supported complementary measure: natural-resource allocation, Great Green Wall/development, or sustainable support to the G-5 Sahel Joint Force.
support_quotes: That obviously requires better allocation of natural resources.
Supporting the G-5 Sahel means providing its Joint Force with the predictable and sustainable logistical and financial support it needs from the United Nations

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: France supported a Council role in assessing and preventing climate-related security risks. Military and peacekeeping deployments alone were insufficient: longer-term responses also needed to understand how climate and crises reinforce each other and strengthen resilience. One complementary measure was predictable, sustainable UN logistical and financial support for the G-5 Sahel Joint Force, alongside development and climate action.
reference_notes: Do not attribute the preceding US PREPARE commitment on page 12 to France. Numbers are optional and not rewarded.

policy_items.question: An analyst writes: “India objected to a Security Council climate role because it denied that climate change could exacerbate conflict.” Assess this characterization against India’s 9 December 2021 statement. Explain its institutional preference and the qualification in its position.

criteria.description: Identify the UNFCCC/COP process as the preferred inclusive, consensus-based forum; explain concern about creating an alternative Council platform.
support_quotes: Let us not deviate from an established and inclusive process of decision-making, with all developing countries participating, and attempt to create an alternative platform for climate change.

criteria.description: Explicitly recognize that India acknowledged climate impacts and exacerbation of conflicts; reject the analyst’s absolute denial.
support_quotes: While we recognize the fact that climate change has impacted the lives of people and exacerbated conflicts in many places

criteria.description: Preserve India’s objection to reducing conflicts to a climate-only explanation or treating a direct/security link as established; frame this as India’s argument rather than an independently verified scientific conclusion.
support_quotes: viewing conflicts only through the prism of climate change presents a misleading perspective.
The oversimplification of causes of conflict will not help to resolve them

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: That characterization is too strong. India acknowledged that climate change had affected lives and exacerbated conflicts. It objected to viewing conflict only through that lens and argued against a separate climate-security platform in the Council. It preferred the UNFCCC/COP process, emphasizing inclusive participation by developing countries and consensus-based decisions.
reference_notes: Accept UNFCCC or a clearly identified UN climate convention process; exact wording is unnecessary. Do not substitute Russia’s adjacent statement for India’s.

policy_items.question: Summarize the UK’s position on climate-security reporting and participation on 9 December 2021, including what it said about the draft before the Council. Does this statement also establish that the UK had approved binding national carbon quotas imposed by the Council?

criteria.description: Explain support for comprehensive UN reporting on climate/security links and a role for the Security Council.
support_quotes: we need the United Nations system to report comprehensively on the links between climate and security
all parts of the United Nations, including the Security Council, have a critical role to play

criteria.description: Include meaningful participation of women and girls, not merely treating them as victims.
support_quotes: we wholeheartedly support a fully inclusive approach, in particular with respect to women and girls
so that they can play a meaningful role.

criteria.description: Report explicit support for the draft submitted to the Council.
support_quotes: Therefore, we support the draft resolution submitted to the Council as an important first step.

criteria.description: State that approval of Council-imposed binding national carbon quotas is not established by this statement.

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: The UK wanted comprehensive UN reporting on climate-security links and a role for the Council. It supported meaningful participation by women and girls and explicitly supported the draft before the Council as a first step. The statement does not establish approval of Council-imposed binding national carbon quotas.
reference_notes: The source contains an announced draft-support position; this is not a prediction without a prior announcement. The quota proposal is an authored probe, not a historical claim.

policy_items.question: What institutional response to climate change did Brazil prefer in its 9 December 2021 statement, and why? Include both its view of climate-related harms and its proposed practical priority.

criteria.description: Explain preference for the inclusive UNFCCC forum, respect for mandates, and avoiding duplication or moving the climate agenda to the Council.
support_quotes: We must strive to avoid duplication of work and ensure that specific mandates and responsibilities within the United Nations system are respected.
having a clearly established mandate and adequate tools and mechanisms to do so.

criteria.description: Acknowledge climate-related resource depletion, disruption, tension or displacement; do not portray Brazil as denying all climate–insecurity connections.
support_quotes: the depletion of resources, aggravated by severe droughts, are some of the factors exacerbating tensions and pushing populations to migrate.

criteria.description: Identify timely/scaled climate finance by developed countries to support developing countries and existing commitments as a practical priority.
support_quotes: The mobilization, scaling-up and timely delivery of financing by developed nations are the need of the hour to support developing countries affected by climate change.

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: Brazil preferred handling the climate agenda through the inclusive UNFCCC process, respecting mandates and avoiding duplication or reallocating the agenda to the Council. It nevertheless acknowledged that drought and depleted resources could worsen tensions and displacement. Its practical priority was timely, increased financing by developed countries to support developing countries and climate commitments.
reference_notes: Brazil was a speaker at this meeting, but it was not a Council member for the 13 December vote. There is no Brazilian action label for this event.

policy_items.question: A memo attributes the 27 September 2022 Council President’s closing national statement to a unanimous Security Council position. Is that attribution warranted? State the position on annexation and continued support for Ukraine that the statement actually establishes, and whether it specifies an exact financial pledge.

criteria.description: Identify the speaker as acting in the national capacity of France, not conveying unanimous Council agreement.
support_quotes: I shall now make a statement in my capacity as the representative of France.

criteria.description: Report France’s rejection/non-recognition of Russia’s illegal annexation attempts.
support_quotes: France will never recognize those illegal annexation attempts by Russia.

criteria.description: Report continued support for Ukraine for as long as needed to uphold independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.
support_quotes: France will continue to provide Ukraine with the support it needs for as long as is necessary in order to ensure respect for its independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

criteria.description: State that this statement does not specify an exact financial pledge.

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: No. The President explicitly switched to speaking as France’s representative; that is not a unanimous Council decision. France said it would not recognize Russia’s illegal annexation attempts and would continue supporting Ukraine for as long as needed to protect its independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity. No exact financial pledge is specified.
reference_notes: The archived English record says “Kharkiv” in its territory list on page 17. Preserve the source; do not silently correct it or use that list as an independently verified geography target.

policy_items.question: What position had the UK publicly expressed on 27 September 2022 about the referendums in occupied Ukrainian regions and the draft put forward by the United States and Albania? Distinguish a stated position at that meeting from a later recorded vote.

criteria.description: Explain rejection of the referendums as illegal/illegitimate or coercive, inconsistent with Ukrainian sovereignty/territorial integrity.
support_quotes: Any referendums held under those conditions, at the barrel
Russia’s holding of sham referendums in the Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhya and Kherson regions of Ukraine is an egregious violation of Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity

criteria.description: Report the UK’s call to support the US/Albania draft.
support_quotes: support the draft resolution the United States and Albania have brought forward today.

criteria.description: Explicitly distinguish the 27 September public support statement from evidence of the eventual recorded vote on 30 September; do not present that later vote as established by the speech.

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: On 27 September the UK rejected the referendums as illegitimate and contrary to Ukrainian sovereignty and territorial integrity, pointing to coercive conditions. It urged support for the draft brought forward by the United States and Albania. This establishes an announced position at that meeting, not the eventual recorded vote on 30 September.
reference_notes: The speech does not cite S/2022/720 by symbol; link to the proposal context is retrospective and does not certify that every word of the later archived draft was fixed on 27 September.

policy_items.question: Using only India’s 27 September 2022 statement, summarize its proposed way forward and its stated principles and assistance priorities. Does that statement establish a definite Y, N or A vote on S/2022/720 three days later?

criteria.description: Include immediate cessation of hostilities and dialogue/diplomacy or a return to negotiation.
support_quotes: India has repeatedly called for an immediate cessation of hostilities and has underscored the need to resolve the ongoing conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.

criteria.description: Include international law/UN Charter and sovereignty/territorial integrity.
support_quotes: We firmly believe that the global order should be anchored in international law, the Charter of the United Nations and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States.

criteria.description: Include humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and economic distress/support in the global South from food/fuel/fertilizer costs.
support_quotes: we provide both humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and economic support to some of our neighbours in the global South
the escalating costs of food, fuel and fertilizer

criteria.description: State that this speech does not establish a definite later Y/N/A vote; do not equate A with model uncertainty.

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: India called for an immediate end to hostilities and a return to dialogue and diplomacy, while affirming international law, the UN Charter, sovereignty and territorial integrity. It described humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and economic support for neighbours in the global South facing food, fuel and fertilizer costs. That speech does not establish a definite Y, N or A vote on the later draft.
reference_notes: The historical action reference is separate. Even a correctly recalled later abstention fails this question if asserted as established by this speech.

policy_items.question: Consider an authored scenario, not an observed negotiation: a future referendum includes independent observers and unrestricted expression. Based on Brazil’s 27 September 2022 statement, would adding those features automatically establish Brazilian recognition of the result? Explain the relevant conditions, Brazil’s assessment of the then-current referendums, and what remains undetermined.

criteria.description: Distinguish the general right of self-determination/possible legitimate use of referendums from approval of every referendum.
support_quotes: the holding of referendums was the means chosen for peoples to express their free will.
Its validity, however, depends on certain conditions.

criteria.description: Mention freedom to express a will under conflict conditions and transparency, expression or independent monitoring; two procedural additions alone do not settle all conditions.
support_quotes: It is unreasonable to assume that populations in areas in conflict are able to freely express their will.
conducted in a transparent manner, without restrictions on the freedom of expression and with the possibility of monitoring by independent observers.

criteria.description: Describe Brazil’s negative assessment of the current referendums and its commitment to territorial integrity or ceasefire/negotiations.
support_quotes: Far from expressing the will of the people
Brazil stands by the principles of respecting the territorial integrity and political unity of sovereign and independent States.

criteria.description: State that recognition of the hypothetical result is not established; do not invent an automatic recognition commitment or a historical vote for the scenario.

policy_items.authored_worked_answer: No automatic recognition follows. Brazil accepted self-determination and the possible legitimate use of referendums, but conditioned validity on a genuinely free choice, transparency, freedom of expression and independent monitoring. It questioned whether people in conflict areas could freely express their will, criticized the current referendums and reaffirmed territorial integrity. Observers and unrestricted expression address some concerns; the statement does not establish recognition of this hypothetical result.
reference_notes: A qualified answer may discuss a more credible procedure, provided it does not invent a commitment to recognition. This scenario has no historical action gold label.

universal_checks.no_unsupported_commitment: No material invented policy, vote, amount, concession or obligation, even if the required points are also present.
universal_checks.correct_attribution: No material misattribution to another country, speaker or institutional capacity.
universal_checks.correct_time_and_scope: No material use of a later event as if established by the dated source; hypothetical events remain hypothetical.

scoring_rule: All item criteria and universal checks must be met. Empty answers fail. Unratable ratings remain unresolved, never passes. Show coverage and components alongside strict pass.
acceptable_variants: Equivalent paraphrases and supported alternatives pass. Exact phrases, national accent/style and agreement with the evaluator’s politics are not targets.
bounded_absence_rule: Not established means absent from the complete selected statement, not proved absent from every possible historical source. Review the full statement, not just one quote.
